name: James Smith
chief_complaint: Severe central chest pain for 3 hours
opening_statement: I've been having really bad chest pain since this morning. It started about 3 hours ago while I was mowing the lawn. The pain is crushing, right in the middle of my chest, and it's been going down my left arm. I feel sweaty and a bit sick in the stomach.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and distressed, speaking in short sentences due to pain, appears pale and diaphoretic

symptoms.onset: 3 hours ago, sudden onset while mowing lawn
symptoms.location: Retrosternal, radiating to left arm and jaw

rag_citation.snippet: Typical presentation includes central chest pain with radiation to left arm, jaw, or epigastrium, associated with diaphoresis and nausea

symptoms.onset: Started with chest pain 3 hours ago

rag_citation.snippet: Autonomic symptoms including diaphoresis are common in STEMI, particularly in inferior wall infarctions due to vagal stimulation
Inferior wall MI commonly presents with nausea and vomiting due to increased vagal tone and diaphragmatic irritation
Dyspnoea may indicate left ventricular dysfunction or early heart failure complicating acute MI

past_medical_history.management: Metformin 1000mg BD, HbA1c last checked 6 months ago was 7.2%

family_history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 58. Mother has Type 2 Diabetes and hypertension, alive at 82. One brother with ischaemic heart disease, underwent CABG at age 60.

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker, quit 5 years ago, 30 pack-year history (smoked 1.5 packs/day for 20 years)
social_history.alcohol: Occasional social drinker, 1-2 standard drinks per week
social_history.exercise: Light gardening and walking, usually 30 minutes 3-4 times per week
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in own home, independent with ADLs
social_history.support: Wife present, two adult children living nearby

examination_findings.general: Alert but distressed, pale, diaphoretic, appears stated age

cardiovascular.heart_sounds: S1 S2 present, soft S3 gallop heard, no murmurs

examination_findings.neurological: Alert and oriented, cranial nerves intact, no focal neurological deficit

ecg.findings: ST elevation 2-3mm in leads II, III, aVF. Reciprocal ST depression in leads I, aVL, V2. Sinus bradycardia at 58bpm
ecg.interpretation: Acute inferior wall STEMI with possible right ventricular involvement

troponin.timing: Initial presentation at 3 hours post symptom onset

chest_xray.findings: Mild pulmonary vascular congestion, heart size upper limit of normal, no acute consolidation

bedside_glucose.interpretation: Mildly elevated in context of acute stress response

actions: Call Code STEMI/activate cardiac catheterisation laboratory
Dual antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin 300mg PO STAT + Ticagrelor 180mg PO STAT (or Clopidogrel 600mg if ticagrelor contraindicated)
Anticoagulation: Heparin bolus 60 units/kg IV (max 4000 units) followed by infusion
Morphine 2.5-5mg IV for pain relief, titrate to effect
Antiemetic: Metoclopramide 10mg IV
High-flow oxygen if SpO2 <94% (target 94-98%)
IV access x2, bloods including troponin, FBC, UEC, coagulation studies, lipids, HbA1c
Continuous cardiac monitoring
Primary PCI within 90 minutes of first medical contact (Class I recommendation)
Right ventricular leads (V4R) if inferior STEMI to assess RV involvement
Cautious fluid resuscitation if RV involvement confirmed (avoid excessive preload reduction)
Consider temporary pacing if high-degree AV block develops
Dual antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin 100mg daily lifelong + Ticagrelor 90mg BD for 12 months
High-intensity statin: Atorvastatin 80mg nocte
ACE inhibitor: Continue/uptitrate Perindopril, target dose 8-10mg daily
Beta-blocker: Metoprolol 25-50mg BD, uptitrate as tolerated
Cardiac rehabilitation referral (MBS item 10951)
Lifestyle modification counselling
Optimize diabetes and hypertension management
Echocardiogram to assess LV function and regional wall motion
MBS item 38215 for emergency coronary angiography
MBS item 38218 for PCI with stent
PBS Authority prescription for ticagrelor (restricted benefit - acute coronary syndrome)
Cardiac rehabilitation program (MBS items 10951, 10952, 10953)
NDSS registration if not already enrolled for diabetes management support

critical_errors.error: Failure to recognize STEMI and activate cardiac catheterisation laboratory within 10 minutes
critical_errors.rationale: Time is myocardium - delays in reperfusion therapy directly correlate with mortality and morbidity. Primary PCI should be performed within 90 minutes of first medical contact.

critical_errors.error: Not administering dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor) immediately
critical_errors.rationale: Dual antiplatelet therapy is fundamental to STEMI management and must be given as soon as diagnosis is made, ideally before PCI. Omission significantly increases risk of stent thrombosis and recurrent MI.

critical_errors.error: Administering nitrates or aggressive fluid bolus without assessing for RV involvement
critical_errors.rationale: Inferior STEMI commonly involves RV. RV infarction is preload-dependent; nitrates and excessive diuresis can cause severe hypotension and cardiogenic shock. Must check right-sided leads (V4R) first.

critical_errors.error: Failure to withhold metformin in context of acute MI and potential contrast exposure
critical_errors.rationale: Metformin should be ceased during acute illness and contrast procedures due to risk of lactic acidosis, particularly with renal impairment. Should be held for 48 hours post-PCI with contrast.

critical_errors.error: Not recognizing bradycardia and AV block risk in inferior STEMI
critical_errors.rationale: Inferior STEMI affects RCA which supplies AV node in 90% of patients. Bradycardia and heart block are common; atropine should be readily available. Beta-blockers should be initiated cautiously.

critical_errors.error: Failure to arrange appropriate follow-up including cardiac rehabilitation
critical_errors.rationale: Cardiac rehabilitation (MBS-funded) improves outcomes post-MI through supervised exercise, risk factor modification, and psychosocial support. Omission reduces long-term survival and quality of life.

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Cardiology), Staff Cardiologist, Royal Melbourne Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent case representing classic inferior STEMI presentation. The inclusion of RV involvement considerations and metformin cessation are high-yield teaching points often missed by candidates. ECG findings are realistic with appropriate ST changes and reciprocal depression. Management pathway aligns with current Australian guidelines and MBS items are correctly cited. Critical errors are appropriately weighted - failure to activate cath lab or give DAPT should indeed be auto-fail. The addition of bradycardia awareness in inferior MI is a nice touch that reflects real clinical practice.
fracp_reviews.suggestions: Consider adding a question about comparing PCI vs thrombolysis if PCI not available within 120 minutes, as this is relevant for rural/remote Australian practice.

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Cardiology), Director of Coronary Care, St Vincent's Hospital Sydney
fracp_reviews.comments: Outstanding case for AMC Clinical Examination preparation. The difficulty calibration is spot-on for 'Medium' - diabetes and hypertension as comorbidities with time-critical management makes this appropriately challenging without being unrealistic. The eTG citations are accurate and well-integrated. I particularly appreciate the inclusion of Australian-specific elements: MBS item numbers for PCI, PBS restrictions for ticagrelor, and NDSS reference. The critical error regarding RV assessment before nitrates is frequently encountered in practice and makes this case highly educational. Vital signs showing relative hypotension with bradycardia accurately reflect vagal tone in inferior MI. This case will effectively test candidates on emergency cardiac care while incorporating chronic disease management.
fracp_reviews.suggestions: Nil - this is a comprehensive, clinically accurate case that meets all requirements for AMC examination preparation.

learning_objectives: Recognize classic presentation of acute inferior wall STEMI including autonomic symptoms (nausea, bradycardia) from vagal stimulation
Understand time-critical nature of STEMI management and importance of activating cardiac catheterisation laboratory within 10 minutes of diagnosis
Demonstrate knowledge of dual antiplatelet therapy in ACS: aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor preferred over clopidogrel in STEMI unless contraindicated)
Identify right ventricular involvement in inferior STEMI and understand implications for management (preload dependence, avoiding nitrates/diuretics)
Apply Australian-specific practice: MBS items for PCI, PBS restrictions for antiplatelet agents, cardiac rehabilitation referral pathways
Recognize need to cease metformin in acute MI context and contrast exposure to prevent lactic acidosis
Understand post-MI secondary prevention: high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor, beta-blocker, and lifestyle modification including cardiac rehabilitation
Demonstrate systematic approach to risk factor modification in patient with multiple cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, ex-smoker, family history)
